title: Integrated GM judgement and versatility
summary: Combine structure, dynamics, prophylaxis and calculation at speed, in open, closed, dynamic and technical positions from both sides.

steps.md:
## Integrated judgement

At 2500+ there is no "strategic" or "tactical" position: every decision combines structure, piece activity, the opponent's ideas and concrete lines — quickly. A practical routine for each important move:
1. **What changed?** (opponent's last move, threats)
2. **What does the position require?** (structure-based plan)
3. **What does he want?** (prophylaxis)
4. **Concrete check** of the 2-3 candidates.

**Versatility**: GMs can play any structure from either side. Training it: play your openings from the *other* side in training games, and study model games in structures you avoid.

steps.prompt: White to move (Carlsen-Karjakin, Bilbao 2016). Only one move keeps the balance (Carlsen-Karjakin, 9th Masters Final 2016 2016)
steps.explain: **19.Bg3!** — the bishop retreats to cover the dark squares and the e5-knight's targets; prophylaxis before activity. Engine main line: 19.Bg3 Ng6 20.Kh1 Nde5 21.Bh2 Qa6 22.Qh5 Nd3. (Carlsen-Karjakin, 9th Masters Final 2016 2016; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.prompt: White to move (Kramnik-Topalov, World Championship 2006). Take the right way (Kramnik-Topalov, WCh 2006)
steps.explain: **17.Nxb2!** — the knight recaptures; the resulting position is balanced but other recaptures lose material. Engine main line: 17.Nxb2 Bb5 18.Ne5 Ra7 19.Na4 Bxe2 20.Rfe1 Bh5. (Kramnik-Topalov, WCh 2006; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.prompt: White to move (Korchnoi-Carlsen, Drammen 2004/05). A central break at the right moment (Korchnoi-Carlsen, Smartfish Masters 2004)
steps.explain: **12.d5!** — the pawn sacrifice/exchange opens the long diagonal for the g2-bishop; only this keeps White's advantage. Engine main line: 12.d5 Nxd5 13.Nxd5 Bg5 14.Bxg5 Qxg5 15.Qc1 Qxc1. (Korchnoi-Carlsen, Smartfish Masters 2004; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.prompt: White to move (Kramnik-Topalov 2006). A quiet queenside move (Kramnik-Topalov, WCh 2006)
steps.explain: **21.a4!** — fixing the queenside before the knights invade; integrated judgement in one move: structure, prophylaxis, preparation. Engine main line: 21.a4 Ne4 22.Rdc1 Bf6 23.Rc2 h6 24.Nc6. (Kramnik-Topalov, WCh 2006; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.prompt: White to move (Ding-Nepomniachtchi, World Championship 2023). A pawn sacrifice that changes the evaluation (Ding Liren-Nepomniachtchi, WCh 2023 2023)
steps.explain: **24.e6!** — the pawn cuts the black position in two and keeps the balance; slower moves let Black consolidate. Engine main line: 24.e6 Bg6 25.a4 a5 26.Be4 Bh5 27.Ree1 Nd6 28.Bd3 Bg6. (Ding Liren-Nepomniachtchi, WCh 2023 2023; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.question: Which training best develops stylistic versatility at GM level?
choices: Playing training games and studying model games in structures you normally avoid, from both sides
steps.explain: Versatility comes from experience in unfamiliar structures. Elite players deliberately broaden their repertoire.

steps.md:
## Assignment

- For one month, play your repertoire from the **opposite side** in training games (Play, 25+10) against a strong bot; analyse each game.
- **Guess the move**: one game per week from each world-champion match in the corpus since 2000.
- Write the four-question routine on your scoresheet in training games until it becomes automatic.
